recentItems.title: Why a US startup wants to start mass production of cruise missiles in Germany | DW News
recentItems.description:
US defense startup Covenant plans to build up to 5,000 long-range cruise missiles a year in eastern Germany. The Anthem missile is designed to be cheaper and easier to mass-p roduce than existing systems, reflecting a growing belief that future conflicts may require far larger stockpiles. Reports suggest Germany's Bundeswehr might want to purchase the missile. As Berlin and its allies rethink deterrence after the war in Ukraine, is the era of mass-produced long-range missiles just beginning?

recentItems.title: Republicans are betting their midterm hopes on Trump | DW News
recentItems.description:
Republicans have opened an unprecedented two-day midterm convention in Dallas dubbed "Trumpapalooza," with Donald Trump speaking on both nights of the event. The party is trying to energize Trump's loyal supporters ahead of the November 3 elections, even as polling shows Republicans facing a difficult fight for Congress and Trump's approval rating remains weak. Some Republicans in competitive races have chosen not to attend. We get the latest from DW’s Benjamin Alvarez Gruber in Texas.

recentItems.title: Netanyahu sues Haaretz over report of alleged pre-attack warning | DW News
recentItems.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says he will sue the Haaretz newspaper over its reporting that UAE president Mohammed bin Zayed warned him about a major Hamas attack days before October 7, 2023. Netanyahu denies any such call took place and says official records show no conversation occurred. We discuss what is known, what remains disputed, and why the story has triggered such intense debate ahead of Israel's October 27 election with Haaretz reporter Linda Dayan, and DW Middle East Analyst Shani Rozanes.

recentItems.description:

Could this latest escalation plunge Yemen back into full-scale war? And what's driving it while the conflict with Iran remains unresolved? Brent Goff speaks to Yemen analyst Baraa Shiban.

recentItems.title: Why Canada's trust in the United States may not recover anytime soon | DW News
recentItems.description:
The United States is expanding its trade war with Canada, introducing import bans on products including many alcoholic beverages, some dairy products and motorcycles after Ottawa imposed roughly $20 billion in retaliatory tariffs on US goods. But the economic measures may be only part of the story. Jen Gerson, co-founder of The Line, argues that years of trust between the two neighbors have been damaged and could take a generation to rebuild.
